Interface Mappings

All Known Implementing Classes:
DefaultMappings, SpringMappings
public interface Mappings
Typed front door to a set of Mappings, whatever format they were loaded from.

Compared to the older MappingService this interface is String-typed and returns Optional rather than null, so call sites no longer cast. An unknown mapping name is a programming error and raises IllegalArgumentException; an unknown key within a known mapping yields an empty Optional. Mappings instances can be built programmatically like this: 

var mappings = Mappings.builder()
    .function("oidUri", s -> !s.isEmpty() && Character.isDigit(s.charAt(0)) ? "urn:oid:" + s : s)
    .load("classpath:/META-INF/map/atna2fhir.mapping.xml")
    .build();

String uri = mappings.map("atnaCodingSystem", "DCM").orElseThrow();
Since:
6.0

    • mappingsFor

      List<Mapping> mappingsFor(String keySystem, String valueSystem)
      Finds mappings by the code systems they translate between, rather than by name.

      A caller holding a code to translate knows which code system it is in and which one it wants, not what the mapping happens to be called - which is the shape of FHIR's ConceptMap/$translate, and the only way to reach a mapping read from a source that names itself, such as a ConceptMap resource. Either argument may be null for "any", so passing only a key system finds every mapping that translates out of it.

      This is a scan over the registered mappings, not an index: resolve the mapping once and keep it, rather than calling this per message.

      Parameters:
      keySystem - identifier of the key code system, or null for any
      valueSystem - identifier of the value code system, or null for any
      Returns:
      the matching mappings, in registration order

    • mappingFor

      default Optional<Mapping> mappingFor(String keySystem, String valueSystem)
      Where a CompositeMapping matches together with some of its parts, the composite stands for them: it answers for all of them, so asking the whole of a ConceptMap by its source system finds the ConceptMap rather than failing on its groups.
      Parameters:
      keySystem - identifier of the key code system, or null for any
      valueSystem - identifier of the value code system, or null for any
      Returns:
      the single mapping translating between the two systems, empty if there is none
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if several mappings translate between them, since picking one of them would be arbitrary - use mappingsFor(String, String) to see them all

    • translate

      default Optional<Translation> translate(String mapping, String key)
      Maps a key like map(String, String), and says which code system the answer belongs to and how it is displayed - what a caller needs to build a coded value from it.

      The system is that of the mapping which actually answered: a composite answers with the system of the part that had the answer, a delegating fallback with that of the mapping delegated to. An identity fallback answers with the key itself, and so with the key system.

      The default implementation knows none of that and answers with the mapping's value system and no display; DefaultMappings overrides it.

      Parameters:
      mapping - mapping name
      key - left side of the mapping
      Returns:
      the mapped value with its system and display, falling back to the mapping's unmatched behavior
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the mapping name is not registered

    • keys

      Set<String> keys(String mapping)
      Parameters:
      mapping - mapping name
      Returns:
      the keys this mapping translates, in declaration order. A key declared only by a Equivalence.DISJOINT entry is not among them, because it does not translate. The keys of a mapping this one delegates to follow its own, since a lookup asks that mapping for every key this one does not declare; keys that only a fallback such as identity answers are not listed. For a composite they are the keys of all its parts. Changes to the set do not change the mapping
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the mapping name is not registered
